title: Hamza Zahoor's Unbeaten Century Lifts Pakistan Past India in U19 Asia Cup
excerpt: Pakistan recovered from 61 for 5 to chase 208 in Muscat, as Zahoor's 100 not out off 108 balls outshone Arjun Rajput's century for India.
body:
• Pakistan beat India by three wickets in a Group A match of the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup in Muscat, chasing 208 with 11 balls to spare.
  • Hamza Zahoor, batting at number seven, finished unbeaten on 100 off 108 balls after Pakistan had collapsed to 61 for 5, sharing a 107-run sixth-wicket stand with Hasnain Abbas Dar.
  • Arjun Rajput's 107 off 85 balls rescued India from 42 for 4, but captain Lakshya Raichandani admitted India finished 20-30 runs short of a par score.
  • Pakistan top Group A with two wins from two; India next face the UAE on Tuesday, November 10.

Pakistan beat India by three wickets in Muscat on Sunday, as Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten century from number seven carried the defending champions home in a Group A match of the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground. Chasing 209, Pakistan were in deep trouble at 61 for 5 before Zahoor's 100 not out off 108 balls, with 10 fours and 3 sixes, took them to 209 for 7 in 48.1 overs with 11 balls to spare, according to IANS reporting carried by Asia Post.

Zahoor's rescue act

Named Player of the Match, Zahoor came in with the chase collapsing around him. India had removed both openers and then taken three wickets for six runs to leave Pakistan 61 for 5, with the match firmly in India's grasp, MyKhel reported. Zahoor and Hasnain Abbas Dar rebuilt with a 107-run partnership for the sixth wicket in 140 deliveries, Dar contributing a patient 38 off 67 balls while Zahoor took charge of the scoring. When Dar and Mohammad Sayyam fell in quick succession late in the chase, India had a final opening — but Zahoor stayed to the end and struck the winning boundary to complete his century.

"No, there wasn't that much pressure. I was enjoying myself, playing my game and enjoying the game."

— Hamza Zahoor, Player of the Match

Zahoor said he had made up his mind to bat through the innings. "Since I had to go all the way, my mindset was that I would stay till the end and win it. I will go till the last," he said at the post-match presentation. Pakistan captain Farhan Yousaf said he was not surprised by the innings: "I know the ability of the guy. I really appreciate the way he assessed the condition and played according to the situation."

Rajput's lone hand for India

India, electing to bat first after winning the toss, were bowled out for 208 despite a sparkling 107 from Arjun Rajput. India were 42 for 4 at one point, and Rajput's century — 107 off 85 balls, with 11 fours and 5 sixes, according to Jagran Josh's match report — held the innings together, with support from Kavya Patel's 23. Pakistan's bowlers shared the wickets evenly: Ali Raza, Rizwan Ullah and Niqab Shafiq claimed three wickets apiece. For India, Manal Chauhan took 3 for 32 in the chase, but it was not enough once Zahoor settled.

India captain Lakshya Raichandani admitted his side had left runs on the field. "We were 20-30 runs short, but overall there were some good innings from Arjun and a good contribution from KP (Kavya Patel)," he said. "We could have bowled a little bit better. But overall, it was really good — there were a lot of positives from this game, and we will try to take that forward."

What it means

The win was Pakistan's second in two matches and moved them to the top of Group A, while India must regroup quickly. India's next fixture is against the UAE on Tuesday, November 10, and Pakistan go forward with, in Yousaf's words, "full intent" in their next match rather than looking ahead to the semi-finals. For diaspora fans following the next generation of the India-Pakistan rivalry, this was a reminder of how quickly a youth match can turn: two centuries, two collapses, and a wicketkeeper-batter at number seven who insisted, afterwards, that he felt no pressure at all.
